Roger Federer. A Swiss tennis legend who won twenty Grand Slam singles titles and dominated the 2000s and 2010s with an elegant all-court game and unmatched consistency. His record stood as the greatest in tennis history until Rafael Nadal surpassed him, but his influence, grace, and sophisticated style redefined modern tennis. He won twenty Grand Slam singles titles across three decades from 2003 to 2018: eight Australian Opens, six Wimbledons, five US Opens, and one French Open. He held the world number one ranking for a record 310 weeks and reached 27 consecutive Grand Slam semifinals between 2004 and 2010, demonstrating extraordinary consistency. He won 103 career ATP titles, a remarkable achievement of durability and skill, and reached at least one Grand Slam final in 13 consecutive years from 2003 to 2015. Known for his graceful, efficient serve-and-volley style, he won on all surfaces, though Wimbledon with six titles was always his signature tournament. He reached age 36 still competing at the highest level and continued to challenge younger players for titles. He retired in 2022 after playing on the circuit into his late thirties. He rivaled and often lost to Rafael Nadal on clay courts. Their epic 2008 Wimbledon final is universally considered one of tennis's greatest matches ever played.
